messages:
Julian Park: quick PSA — found a canary flow where inspect-mode logs are getting stored without full redaction. happened during last night's canary rollout.
Tara Gomez: damn, repro steps? which canary?
Julian Park: Console canary id cny-47, route /v1/chat, sampling=1.0 for canary. steps: enable inspect, hit test payload with PII, check s3 prefix `canary-inspect/` — got raw user_email and phone.
Mike Chen: ok are we sure this is before or after the ingestion scrub? could be a race with async scrub job.
Tara Gomez: checked — scrub job kicks, but storage write happens by the canary agent pre-scrub. agent config has `inspect_mode: true` which intentionally bypasses final scrub to preserve context for debugging. that "bypass" is the issue.
Samir Patel: we intentionally allowed unredacted for oncall canaries, but this should be gated to private buckets only and short TTL. how did it end up in regular canary prefix?
Julian Park: config drift — deploy bot used previous template that defaulted to public-canary-prefix.
Anita Rao: propose immediate mitigation: add a server-side hard guard that enforces `redact_level: strict` for any canary with `inspect_mode` unless tenant_flag=allowed_inspect. and auto-move existing objects into quarantine + scrub.
Mike Chen: agree. we need a code change + console toggle. low-risk patch: in ingress pipeline add check: if (is_canary && inspect_mode && !tenant_allowlist) then set redact_level=strict and set storage_prefix=quarantine.
Tara Gomez: also want telemetry so we can track how often this would have triggered in the wild. add metric `canary.inspect_unredacted_attempts{tenant}` and a dashboard heatmap.
Samir Patel: UX question — support engineers rely on inspect-mode to see raw context. if we force strict redact it defeats purpose. maybe provide a secure inspect path: ephemeral access in Console > Observability > Canaries, with time-limited credentials + audit log.
Anita Rao: yep. implement short-term hard guard + ticket to build secure inspect UI. short-term checklist: 1) patch ingress guard (Mike), 2) script to move + scrub existing objects (Tara), 3) flip console canary default to `inspect_mode:false` (Julian), 4) add metric and alert (Samir).
sre-bot: deploy started: canary-scrub-guard v0.1 by Mike Chen — CI passed, rolling to infra-canaries. :rocket:
Mike Chen: patch PR in flight: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/842 — adds ingress guard and quarantine mover. please review.
Tara Gomez: running scrub script on cny-47 prefix now, ETA ~12m. logging results to #incidents for audit.
Julian Park: tagging @anita for policy approval to make this guard permanent. also we should update docs: Console > Canary runbook + data handling appendix.
Anita Rao: approved for now. will draft policy note about allowed_inspect tenants and requirements (signed NDA, S3 private, KMS).
Samir Patel: one more: add per-route sampling UI warning when enabling inspect-mode that shows potential PII risk and requires checkbox ack. small UX win.
Tara Gomez: +1. also add double-confirm in API (header `X-Inspect-Confirm: true`) so scripted canaries are less likely to slip.
Julian Park: thanks all. I'll follow up with postmortem if scrub reveals more.
Samir Patel: thanks — appreciate quick triage :thumbsup:
Mike Chen: will keep monitoring. once deployment stabilizes I'll post rollback plan if anything weird shows up.
Tara Gomez: scrub finished: 42 objects moved, 0 failures. uploading scrub audit to #incidents.
Julian Park: closing loop here for now. next steps tracked in GH issue 2134.
Anita Rao: closing note — we should add an alert that fires if any canary prefix contains >0 unredacted matches for email/phone via nightly scan.
Samir Patel: good call, file a small RFC and we can schedule in next sprint.
